title: 12.1 Cross Sections of Solids

icans: I can tell whether a solid is a polyhedron and name it.
I can use Euler’s Theorem to find the number of faces, vertices, or edges.
I can describe the shape of a cross section of a solid.

vocab: a solid that is bounded by ___________, called faces
a polygon that forms a side of a _____________
a segment where two faces of a _____________ meet
a point where three or more edges of a _____________ meet
the _______________ of a plane and a solid

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Discovery: count faces, vertices, and edges

blocks.p: Count the faces (F), vertices (V), and edges (E) of each solid.
F + V is always ______ more than E.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Prisms and pyramids: a prism has two congruent, parallel _______________; a pyramid has one base, and its lateral faces meet at a _______________.

blocks.stem:
Tell whether each solid is a polyhedron. If it is, name it.
a.  two parallel pentagon bases and five rectangle faces
b.  a cone
c.  a square base and four triangle faces that meet at a point

notes: Euler’s Theorem: for any polyhedron, F + V = _______________

blocks.stem: A polyhedron has 12 faces and 30 edges. How many vertices does it have?
Find the number of faces, vertices, and edges of the hexagonal prism. Check that Euler’s Theorem holds.

notes: Cross section: the shape formed where a _______________ slices through a solid.

blocks.stem:
Describe the shape of each cross section.
a.  a cube cut by a plane parallel to a face (shown)
b.  a cylinder cut by a vertical plane through the centers of its bases
c.  a cone cut by a plane parallel to its base
A plane cuts off one corner of a cube, as shown. What shape is the cross section?
Count the faces, vertices, and edges of a square pyramid. Show that Euler’s Theorem holds.

Describe the cross section of a square pyramid cut by
a.  a plane parallel to its base
b.  a vertical plane through its vertex and the midpoints of two opposite base edges

tickets.stem: A polyhedron has 8 faces and 12 vertices. How many edges does it have?
A cube is cut by a plane parallel to one of its faces. What shape is the cross section?
Is a cylinder a polyhedron? Explain.
